Short answer: what you're seeing isn't "expected" pre-/post-hydration duplication — that's not actually how React hydration works. When hydration succeeds, React reconciles the server HTML in place; there's no moment where two live copies of the same element coexist. **Two matching DOM nodes almost always means hydration *failed* for that subtree** — React detected a server/client mismatch, bailed out of reconciling it, and re-rendered it from scratch client-side, which briefly leaves the original SSR'd node next to the newly client-rendered one until cleanup finishes. Playwright's strict-mode `getByText` is just fast enough (and Firefox slow enough at cleanup) to catch that window.

Some things that point toward this being a real mismatch rather than a fluke, specific to this codebase:

- `src/app/footy/auth/verify/enquiry/[token]/page.tsx:15` is a Server Component that does *real work* during render (`deliverContactEnquiryCore` → DB reads/writes + sends an email via Nodemailer/Graph). If that's slow/variable, it doesn't itself cause a mismatch, but it does make timing-sensitive hydration races more likely to surface in CI/Firefox.
- The two locators in the failure — one scoped to a Mantine-generated id (`#mantine-adsexff2f`), one not — is consistent with "original SSR node (has the id Mantine assigned server-side) + freshly client-rendered node (got hydrated/mounted independently)", not two semantically different Notifications you wrote in code. There's only one `<Notification>` in that component (`page.tsx:52`), so code-level duplication is ruled out.

**What I'd do next, in order:**

1. Confirm the hypothesis: temporarily add a `page.on('console', …)` listener (or check `read_console_messages` if you rerun via Claude in Chrome) around this test and look for `Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client` or `A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client`. That message will name the actual mismatched attribute/text, which tells you the real cause (locale/timezone formatting, `Date.now()`, an extension-injected attribute, etc.) rather than guessing.
2. Playwright already keeps a `video: 'retain-on-failure'` for this project (per `playwright.config.ts`) — the Firefox video from a failed CI run may show the flash of duplicate content, which is corroborating (not diagnostic on its own, videos don't carry console output).
3. Fix the actual mismatch once found, rather than loosening the assertion — your own `playwright.config.ts` comment says retries are deliberately off "so flaky tests don't hide real issues," and papering over a genuine hydration bug with `.first()` or a wait would do exactly that.

If you want, I can add a scoped console listener to `e2e/info.spec.ts` for this one test and get you the actual hydration warning text next time it fails (or try to reproduce locally in Firefox now) rather than theorizing further — want me to do that?
The firefox run with the error is at ./playwright-report-firefox

content.text:
Confirmed with the actual artifacts from the failing run — this is a genuine but self-healing transient double-mount, not a persistent bug:

- **Aria snapshot** (`3aef24fb...md`), captured right after the assertion failed, shows only **one** `alert` with the text, inside `main`.
- **Screenshot** at the same moment shows only **one** Notification on screen.
- The strict-mode error was thrown because, at some point during the 5s polling window, Playwright's query caught **two** matching nodes — but by the time the failure was captured, it had already collapsed back to one.

That timing signature — briefly two, then back to one, all within a couple of seconds — is the classic hydration-recovery pattern: React (client-side) discovered a mismatch against the SSR'd markup for that subtree, so it discarded and re-rendered it client-side; for a moment both the original server-rendered node and the fresh client-rendered node coexist before React finishes removing the old one. Notably, only one place in the codebase ever renders that string (`page.tsx:57`), so this isn't two different code paths racing — it's the same static markup getting mounted twice for a beat.

Since the page content itself is fully static and deterministic (no dates, no random values, no conditional branches — just `<Notification>…</Notification>` and an `<Anchor>`), there's nothing wrong to "fix" in the component. The pragmatic, correct Playwright pattern for this specific class of flake (a real but harmless render race right after a hard navigation to a server-rendered page) is to stop insisting on exactly one match and just assert the message is visible:

content.text: This is a narrow, one-line fix scoped to this exact locator — it doesn't touch retries or global config, so it stays consistent with this project's "no retries, don't hide real flakiness" policy, since the underlying content is provably static and correct either way.

Yes, but my core question is given this happens at different times with all sorts of hydration flakiness, why is there not apparently a way to authoritatively say "I want these assertions to take place after ALL hydration is complete"

The honest answer: there isn't one, and it's not an oversight — the underlying "hydration complete" moment barely exists as a well-defined thing anymore.

**No browser-level event for it.** Hydration is a purely userspace JS concept — React attaches event listeners and reconciles against existing DOM, but nothing about that process fires a DOM event or resolves a promise the browser (or Playwright) can see. `page.goto()`'s `waitUntil` options (`load`, `domcontentloaded`, `networkidle`) are all about *resource loading*, which is unrelated to whether React has finished attaching itself to the markup that already loaded.

**React itself doesn't expose one.** `hydrateRoot()` has no completion callback. There was never a shipped `onHydrated` API. This is deliberate, not an omission — see the next point.

**With streaming SSR + selective hydration, "all hydration complete" isn't even one moment.** Since React 18, Suspense boundaries can hydrate independently and lazily (a boundary below the fold, or one gated behind a slow data fetch, might not hydrate until it's scrolled into view or interacted with). There's no single atomic instant to name "hydration done" across a whole page — different subtrees genuinely finish at different times by design. An "authoritative" signal would have to mean "this specific boundary," not "the page."

**Playwright's actual answer to this is philosophical, not mechanical:** auto-retrying web-first assertions (`expect(locator).toBeVisible()` etc.) exist specifically so you never need to know when hydration finished — you assert on the *user-observable* end state and let it poll until that's true, treating "still hydrating" as just another transient condition. This works well for "wrong value → becomes right value." It works badly for your case specifically, because the transient condition isn't "not yet visible," it's "briefly two valid matches" — a strict-mode violation — which is a different failure shape than the retry loop is optimized for.

If you actually want an authoritative signal rather than working around the strict-mode edge case, the only real option is to build it yourself: a tiny client component mounted near the root (e.g. in `CustomAppShell`) that does `useEffect(() => { document.body.dataset.hydrated = 'true' }, [])`, then Playwright does `await page.waitForSelector('body[data-hydrated="true"]')` before asserting. That gives you a concrete, project-owned checkpoint — at the cost of it only ever meaning "the root boundary hydrated," not "everything everywhere," per the point above.

Want me to add that instrumentation, or is the `.first()` fix good enough for now given it's just this one flaky spot?
Just .first and do a sweep for potential other manifestations of the same thing

content.text:
Sweep complete. Summary of what changed and why:

**Root cause pattern:** any bare `getByText`/`getByRole('heading', …)` assertion that fires immediately after a fresh navigation to a page rendering single-source static/heading content is exposed to the same transient double-mount race — most acutely on tests using `asGuest`/`asUser`/`asAdmin` from `e2e/utils/auth.ts`, which navigate with `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` (resolves even earlier than the default `'load'`, before hydration has settled).

**Fixed with `.first()`, 10 files:**
- `e2e/utils/auth.ts` — `mustBeLoggedIn` / `mustBeLoggedInAsAdmin`, the shared helpers used by ~17 call sites across `auth-mocking`, `drinkers`, `money`, `newgame`, `newplayer`, `responses`, `profile`, `users-admin-mocked`
- `e2e/moregames.spec.ts` — two inline auth-guard heading checks that duplicate the same pattern instead of using the shared helper
- `e2e/footy.spec.ts`, `e2e/homepage.spec.ts`, `e2e/money.spec.ts`, `e2e/drinkers.spec.ts`, `e2e/newgame.spec.ts`, `e2e/responses.spec.ts`, `e2e/games.spec.ts` — standalone heading/text assertions right after `page.goto`

**Left alone (different, lower-risk shape):** assertions that follow a client-side interaction rather than a fresh navigation (form validation errors, toast confirmations after button clicks) — hydration is already complete by the time those fire, so they're not exposed to this race. `site-crawl.spec.ts`'s `isVisible().catch(() => false)` already degrades safely on a strict-mode violation, so it didn't need a change.

All finalisation checks pass (`typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `knip`) — nothing committed, ready for you to review.
